messages:
incbot: :rotating_light: PAGER — P0: serving-runtime crashlooping on us-west-2 GPU pool (production-serving). Affected: hosted API routes, increased 502/503 responses. Pager routed to @sam (oncall). Links: <https://dash.redwood.internal/incidents/1758008123>

sam (oncall): Ack. Creating incident thread here. Observed customer reports via support. I'll start triage — pinging eng-runtime and eng-sre.

mica (eng-runtime): Looking at container stdout/stderr — repeated SIGSEGV inside native runtime when loading custom kernels. Sample tail:

```
2025-11-02T10:12:45Z runtime: loading libcustom_kernels.so
2025-11-02T10:12:45Z runtime: initializing cuda subsystems
2025-11-02T10:12:46Z runtime: segfault (signal 11) at 0x00007f...
#0 0x7fxx in custom_kernel_init()
#1 0x55xx in runtime_start()
```

mica (eng-runtime): This started ~2h after a runtime build rolled (build: bld_2025_11_02_08:10). Might be a bad kernel binary or incompatible CUDA driver. Trying to reproduce locally on an identical AMI.

raj (eng-sre): Kube shows CrashLoopBackOff on 8 pods across 3 nodes. Crash counts increasing. `kubectl describe pod` shows restart count 47 for one pod. dmesg on node shows repeated GPU errors: `NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 86` and GPU reset messages.

raj (eng-sre): Node-level summary:
- node-usw2-gpu-14: repeated GPU resets
- node-usw2-gpu-16: OOM events <kernel log shows oom_killer invoked on pid 3245>

sam (oncall): Immediate mitigations: (1) isolate affected pool, (2) shift traffic off GPU-heavy routes to CPU fallback variant if possible, (3) attempt non-disruptive env toggle to disable custom kernels. Doing (2) and (3) now.

mica (eng-runtime): Quick test: setting `REDWOOD_RUNTIME_DISABLE_CUSTOM_KERNELS=1` avoids loading libcustom_kernels.so. Patching deployment env for a single replica to validate.

```
kubectl -n production patch deployment serving-runtime -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"runtime","env":[{"name":"REDWOOD_RUNTIME_DISABLE_CUSTOM_KERNELS","value":"1"}]}]}}}}'
```

mica (eng-runtime): Patched one pod and restarted. Pod came up cleanly on GPU node without segfault, appears to initialize but falls back to CPU path for kernels.

deploy-bot: rollout status: 1/1 updated, pod ready.

sam (oncall): Good. Rolling this patch across the rest of the pool in a controlled manner (+1 pod at a time) to avoid mass evictions.

liz (support): Customer impact: AcmeCorp and BetaApps reported 502/503 since ~10:12 UTC. AcmeCorp production traffic is degraded; we've opened tickets and notified their engineering lead. Latency for CPU fallback estimated 2-3x; they asked for ETA to full restore.

ana (product): Need messaging: short note on status and mitigation and expected perf hit. Also confirm which customers are on Dedicated vs Hosted so we can prioritize.

mica (eng-runtime): Rolling env patch to remaining pods now. Plan: full pool patch (disable custom kernels) then rebuild and revert later once we have a fixed kernel binary. Created issue: RWD-INC-1758008123 with build id and logs.

raj (eng-sre): Recommend cordoning node-usw2-gpu-14 and draining if GPU is flapping. Doing `kubectl cordon node-usw2-gpu-14` then `kubectl drain --force --ignore-daemonsets` after patch is applied to avoid restarts on problematic hardware.

sam (oncall): Proceed with cordon/drain for the 2 nodes with most resets. Keep one healthy node for control.

mica (eng-runtime): Reproducer notes: reproduces when CUDA driver is 525.xx + our kernel binary built against 530. Likely ABI mismatch. We should check CI matrix and the AMI provisioning script.

mica (eng-runtime): Temp mitigation ticket: disable custom kernels until we can build compatible kernels for 525 drivers and run canary. Revert plan: after kernel rebuild and validation, re-enable env var and roll.

liz (support): Messaging drafted: "We are mitigating a runtime crash affecting model inference for some customers. Traffic has been shifted to a CPU fallback; this reduces errors but increases latency. Engineering is rolling a fix; we'll update in 30 minutes." Ready to send to impacted customers.

sam (oncall): ETA: short-term mitigation applied. Monitoring for error rate and 5xx. If error rate remains high after full patch, escalate to platform infra for urgent driver roll or node replacement.

mica (eng-runtime): Opening PR to revert the bad runtime build and add a guard in CI to verify CUDA driver compatibility. PR: https://git.redwood/repo/pull/4821

deploy-bot: Canary rollout complete: 6/6 pods patched. No segfaults observed in last 12m on patched pods.

raj (eng-sre): Node drains completed for two nodes. Replaced with new instances built from AMI with CUDA 530 to test. Monitoring GPU Xid events.

sam (oncall): Inc status: partial mitigation — crashloops stopped for patched pods, CPU fallback active. Impact: degraded latency for some customers. Next steps: build compatible kernel, validate on canary nodes, then re-enable kernels and roll.

mica (eng-runtime): Assigning follow-up to `runtime-kernel` team. Root cause likely ABI mismatch between custom kernels and deployed CUDA driver. Recording reproduction steps and logs in linked ticket.

noah (next-oncall): Acked handoff time 1758011700. I'll monitor overnight and coordinate final revert if ready. Handoff notes: mitigation=env disable, canary stable, rebuild in progress, contact oncall-sre if Xid events reappear.

sam (oncall): Handoff complete. If anyone sees recurring segfaults, escalate immediately. Closing active pager for now; keeping incident open for postmortem and customer comms.

incbot: Incident status updated -> mitigated. Postmortem owner: mica (eng-runtime). Timeline placeholder: https://dash.redwood.internal/incidents/1758008123/postmortem

liz (support): I'll follow up with impacted customers with the mitigation update and expected timeline for full restore. :white_check_mark:

mica (eng-runtime): Adding logs + `gdb` backtrace and exact offending symbol to the issue. Also adding CI check to run a small glibc/CUDA compatibility matrix during release.

sam (oncall): Thanks team. Leaving thread open for updates; will close after postmortem is drafted.
